title: chat.completions: normalize role tokens, accept stop arrays, and stabilize stream logprobs + tool-call framing
author: Asha Patel
release_notes:
- Add full support for stop as an array (matches OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics)
- Normalize message.role values coming from clients to canonical set: system/user/assistant/tool
- Ensure streamed delta events include consistent logprobs when requested
- Introduce streaming framing shim to keep function/tool-call boundaries in partial responses
- Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in flag to enable strict OpenAI-mode for legacy clients
description:
Motivation: customers using the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions endpoint reported mismatches in behavior vs public OpenAI: stop sequences passed as arrays were ignored in some paths, roles from third-party SDKs (e.g. 'user_message', 'assistant-v2') were treated as free-form tokens causing downstream routing bugs, and streamed deltas did not reliably surface logprobs or tool-call boundaries. This PR brings parity for common OpenAI shapes and stabilizes streaming for tool/function calling.

What this PR does: 1) Accepts `stop` as either a string or an array of strings for both non-streaming and streaming requests; arrays are checked before string fallback. 2) Introduces a canonicalizer for incoming message.role values (mapping known aliases to system|user|assistant|tool). 3) Adds consistent inclusion of token-level `logprobs` in streaming deltas when the client requests `logprobs` in the completion params, guaranteeing that final streamed event and non-streaming response match. 4) Implements a lightweight framing shim for tool/function calls during streaming: we emit explicit `tool_call.start` and `tool_call.end` events (internal event type in streaming payloads) so clients can reliably reconstruct tool invocations without waiting for finalization. 5) Tests and updates the OpenAI compat middleware and SDK adapters to exercise these changes.

Compatibility notes: default behavior preserves existing Redwood semantics for clients that do not enable strict OpenAI compatibility mode. The new canonical role mappings are idempotent for standard roles; collisions only arise for exotic aliases and are logged at INFO. Stop-array handling is enabled for all users because it is safe and consistent with real-world usage. Streaming framing is additive and does not change final text outputs.

Testing and verification: unit tests for the canonicalizer, stop-array parsing, and streaming event generator; integration tests that compare /v1/chat.completions (compat) vs the native API for the same prompts; an E2E smoke run against the TypeScript SDK and a small canary in staging with real traffic for 48h.

Rollout plan: feature gates exist behind `OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT` environment flag. Default rollout: enable stop-array & role canonicalization cluster-wide on day 0; enable streaming framing behind the flag, flip for 10% traffic after CI green, expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added (compat matrix)
- [x] SDK adapter updates (ts + py)
- [x] Canary plan documented

Links: Linear ENG-1764 (compat parity), ENG-1899 (streaming reliability), SUPPORT ticket SUP-742.
commit_summary: 6 commits: refactor compat middleware to centralize role/stop handling; add stop-array parser + tests; streaming: include logprobs in delta frames; introduce tool_call framing events and consumption logic; update TS/Python SDK adapters and docs; add integration tests and canary config.
files_changed: server/serving/streaming/stream_generator.go - include logprobs in deltas + framing hooks
sdk/ts/src/adapters/openai_compat.ts - adopt canonical role inputs and streaming event handling
sdk/python/redwood_openai_compat.py - stop-array acceptance + role mapping (tests updated)
docs/openai_compat.md - updated compatibility notes and migration guidance
tests/integration/compat/parity_matrix.test.ts - add cases for stop arrays and role aliases

Asha Patel: Added streaming stop-array termination test and updated integration script to simulate high-latency token tails.
Sofia Martinez: The role canonicalization map needs a comment about future collisions and a metric; request adding a metric count for 'role_alias_mapped'.
Asha Patel: Added role_alias_mapped counter and a short note in openai_compat.md explaining mapping policy.
Ethan Boyd: CI flake on linux/arm build in first run; reran CI and fixed a tiny concurrency bug in stream_generator.go related to token buffer reuse.
Cameron Li: Approved after the concurrency fix and added tests.

Watch metrics: errors.openai_compat, streaming.restarts, role_alias_mapped, stop_array_terminations. Canary config in deploy/canary/configs/openai_compat_canary.yaml.
